claims.text: Wear performance of high-entropy-alloy protective coatings is governed by the formation of a stable nanocrystalline grain structure.
A stable nanocrystalline grain structure resists plastic deformation.
A stable nanocrystalline grain structure resists crack propagation.
Alloy composition influences the formation and stability of the nanocrystalline grain structure.
Processing conditions influence the formation and stability of the nanocrystalline grain structure.
The wear-test environment influences the formation or stability of the nanocrystalline grain structure.
Increasing the stability of the nanocrystalline grain structure will improve wear performance.
The hypothesized relationship is intended to hold across varying wear loads, speeds, and environmental conditions, subject to the stability limits of the nanocrystalline structure.
Coatings with an optimized grain structure are expected to outperform coatings without an optimized grain structure.
Wear rate, grain size and structure, plastic deformation, and crack propagation can be measured during controlled wear testing to test the hypothesis.
